title: Utterance decomposition + metadata contradictions — notes and quick heuristics
content:
Notes to self / scratchpad — do not publish yet

Context
- Focus: multi-intent utterances + conflicts between user-supplied fields (metadata) and content. Example domains: chat assistants, form autofill, scheduling, e-comm searches.
- Problem: annotators often disagree when an utterance implies two intents and external metadata (e.g., client timezone, device locale, user profile) points to a conflicting interpretation. We need crisp heuristics to keep labels consistent across labelers and downstream model training.

High-level goals
- Keep labels deterministic and conservative: favor conservative decomposition (only split when both parts are actionable)
- Capture metadata provenance as separate tags, not embedded in intent label if contradictory
- Record explicit "uncertainty reasons" so we can filter for noisy training examples

Quick heuristics (first-pass)
1) Intent split rule: split utterance only when two or more independent actions could be taken by system without additional context.
   - e.g. "Book flight to SFO and remind me to pack" -> split: [book_flight(destination=SFO), set_reminder(note=pack)]
   - e.g. "Find flights to SFO for next week or cheaper options" -> do NOT split; treat as single complex search intent (because actions are alternatives, not sequential).

2) Metadata precedence: when metadata (profile timezone, last-known-city, device-locale) contradicts explicit textual indicators, prioritize explicit text for intent extraction; capture metadata contradiction in a separate field: metadata_conflict_reason.
   - Example: user text: "Schedule call tomorrow 9am" + profile_tz=UTC, device_tz=PST, server_timestamp shows timezone ambiguous. Assume local interpretation: "tomorrow 9am" resolves relative to the user's explicit timezone in message if present; otherwise default to device_tz and flag uncertainty.

3) Ambiguous temporal expressions: label with canonical resolution AND mark resolution_source: [text, profile, device, server_time]. If resolution uses anything other than text, add tag "time_resolution_inferred".

4) When user writes a list where one item is clearly a separate directive and another is descriptive, split only the directive. If both are directives, split both.
   - e.g. "Show me my receipts, I need to expense lunch" -> split into [show_receipts, create_expense(category=food?)]. If second lacks required fields (amount/date) keep as TODO intent with high_abstain flag.

Open/edge cases to decide
- Implicit beneficiaries: "Schedule team sync and tell Tina" -> Is "tell Tina" a separate intent (send_message) or part of schedule instruction (notify attendee)? I think treat as separate intents when target is named and delivery method implied.
- Coreference with metadata: "Cancel my 3pm" + metadata: user has multiple 3pm events. Label as cancel_event with ambiguity flag and include candidate_event_count.
- Partial commands with references to previous context: if utterance lacks explicit slot but context provides it (previous assistant message), annotate slot_source=context and include context_message_id. For users/Drive privacy reasons, we can't include full IDs in public training examples — instead store a hashed context pointer.

Annotation UI suggestions (to reduce noise)
- Provide quick toggles: "split/merge", "mark-metadata-used", "time_resolution_source" dropdown, "uncertainty_reason" free text with quick tags.
- Show short summary of relevant metadata inline (profile city, device tz, last activity) with a one-click "use metadata" button that autofills resolution but also sets metadata_used flag.

Label schema proposal (minimal fields)
- intents: list of {intent_name, slots: list of slot_kv as strings, confidence_tag: low|medium|high}
- decomposition_type: none|consecutive|parallel|alternative
- metadata_used: yes|no
- metadata_conflict_reason: string (optional)
- uncertainty_reasons: list of strings (optional)
- annotations_notes: free text (recommended for borderline cases)

Sample tricky examples and my suggested annotations
1) "Remind me to call mom tomorrow and also set an alarm for 6"
   - intents: [set_reminder(target=mom, time=tomorrow), set_alarm(time=6:00)]
   - decomposition_type: consecutive
   - metadata_used: no

2) "Find cheap hotels in Paris for next week — my card on file is expiring soon"
   - intents: [search_hotels(location=Paris, dates=next_week)]
   - secondary_info: payment_method_warning (NOT an intent) -> add tag "metadata_signal_payment"
   - decomposition_type: none

3) "Move my meeting from noon to 3pm, I'm in PST" + profile says CET
   - intents: [reschedule_event(original_time=12:00, new_time=15:00)]
   - time_resolution: text_annotated_with_tz=PST
   - metadata_used: yes (user explicitly provided tz in text)
   - metadata_conflict_reason: "profile_tz_conflicts_with_text"

4) "Order more toner and check price" -> is this split? Both could be separate actions (create_order, price_check). Preference: split into [order_item(item=toner), check_price(item=toner)] but mark as sequential/parallel? set decomposition_type=parallel (two separate actions).

Annotation quality checks / post-label filters
- If uncertainty_reasons not empty or metadata_conflict_reason present, mark sample for a review pass before using in high-confidence training subset.
- Track inter-annotator disagreement particularly on decomposition decisions. If disagreement rate > 30% on a cohort, create a micro-FAQ with edge examples.

Experiments to run (quick A/B)
- A: conservative labels (no-split unless both actionable) vs B: aggressive split (split whenever two verb phrases). Train separate intent classifiers and compare downstream precision on action extraction. Metrics: F1 per intent, false-positive action triggers in live beta.
- Log dataset velocity: how many examples get metadata_conflict flag weekly? Use as signal to prioritize better metadata collection in product.

Todo / immediate next steps
- Draft a short labeling checklist (one-pager) for crowd labelers with 10 canonical examples + 10 edgecases. (slot: UX ticket for checklist)
- Add UI toggles prototype to the annotation tool: time_resolution dropdown, metadata_used checkbox. (link to UX mock: confluence://ux/utterance-ui-quickmock)
- Create a small adjudication batch of 200 ambiguous utterances (pull from recent production logs) and see annotator agreement under proposed schema.

Random scribbles / heuristics I keep returning to
- Always prefer explicit textual evidence over presumed metadata unless user explicitly references metadata.
- Tag everything that required inference from external profile as "inferred_from_profile" so models can learn to ignore vs rely on that signal.
- Keep decomposition decisions reversible: store a canonical joined-intent representation so we can merge splits later in evaluation.

Questions for the team (ping in doc)
- @Jonah: do we have a quick way to show device_tz in annotation UI today?
- @Priya: for time normalization, are we using duckling or our internal normalizer? Which supports explicit tz hints?

End of scratchpad. Will clean and put formal checklist in shared_drives once we have agreement.
